newsitem.title: INDIA: India insurance workers to strike on December 9.
newsitem.headline: India insurance workers to strike on December 9.

text.p: Nearly 200,000 employees of India's state-run insurance companies will strike on December 9 to protest against government move to privatise the insurance sector, trade union officials said on Tuesday.

Employees of the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) and the General Insurance Corporation (GIC) and their subsidiaries will take part in the one-day strike, P.P. Ravindranathan, secretary of the United Forum of General Insurance Employees, said in a statement.

"The insurance employees have been intensifying their agitation in view of the reported move to introduce a bill in the current session of parliament on the privatisation of the insurance sector," Ravindranathan said in the statement.
India began liberalising trade, industry and banking in 1991 as part of a sweeping programme to dismantle decades of socialist controls.
But so far the insurance sector has not been thrown open to the private sector and all Indian insurance companies are state-owned.
Industry officials say the value of India's insurance industry is about 150 billion rupees ($4.4 bln) and the sector is growing by about 11 percent per year.
Former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao's government set up the Insurance Regulatory Authority in 1995 to draft proposed changes in the laws and suggest ways to open up the industry.
About 22 foreign firms from the U.S., Canada, Switzerland, the Middle East and Japan are making plans to enter the Indian insurance market, insurance sector officials said recently.
"But we are not scared of competition from them," GIC Chairman and Managing Director K. C. Mittal told reporters in Calcutta last week.
